text: He remembered the Great Famine. <break time="0.8s" /> Of his childhood. <break time="0.8s" /> The terrible winter. <break time="0.8s" /> In which his own mother had died. <break time="0.8s" /> That summer. <break time="0.8s" /> The salmon had not come up the rivers. <break time="0.8s" /> And in winter. <break time="0.8s" /> The caribou did not come either. <break time="0.8s" /> The dogs grew so thin. <break time="0.8s" /> That they were nothing but bones. <break time="0.8s" /> And when spring came at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Not one person in ten. <break time="0.8s" /> Was still alive. <break time="0.8s" /> He also remembered a winter day. <break time="0.8s" /> When he and Zing ha. <break time="0.8s" /> His boyhood friend. <break time="0.8s" /> Found strange tracks. <break time="0.8s" /> On a frozen creek. <break time="0.8s" /> Zing ha who later became the cleverest of hunters. <break time="0.8s" /> Would one day fall. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a hole in the ice. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the Yukon. <break time="0.8s" /> But on that day. <break time="0.8s" /> He was only a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was he. <break time="0.8s" /> Who read the story. <break time="0.8s" /> Written in the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> There were the tracks of an old moose. <break time="0.8s" /> And, close beside them. <break time="0.8s" /> The tracks of many wolves. <break time="0.8s" /> Zing ha said that the moose was too old. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep up with its herd. <break time="0.8s" /> And that the wolves had cut it off. <break time="0.8s" /> He also said that the wolves would never leave such a moose. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the end. <break time="0.8s" /> If the moose had stayed close to its herd. <break time="0.8s" /> It would have been much safer. <break time="0.8s" /> But now it had to fight alone.
